| [LIT-001](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-001.md) v2 | Quantum Mechanics can be understood through stochastic optimization on spacetimes | Lindgren & Liukkonen (2019), DOI-10.1038/s41598-019-56357-3. The paper derives a Stueckelberg-type equation i∂φ/∂τ = (1/2m)□φ − Vφ (Eq. 36) from an HJB equation, but only after putting the imaginary unit in twice by hand. The first i is a factor √g = i multiplying the Lagrangian; standard relativity uses √(−g) = 1. The second is a complex "variance" σ² = i/m (Eq. 29), chosen so that the Hopf–Cole substitution J = log φ linearizes the equation. The linearization itself is the standard λ = σ²·(control cost) condition. The Schrödinger equation (Eq. 43) then comes from c → ∞ plus complex conjugation. The Dirac equation is not derived, and the "Klein–Gordon equation" (Eq. 40) has 2mV where m² should be. | Rejected — read in full 2026-09-25 ([NOTE-003](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-003.md)); the claim that the i comes from the Minkowski metric depends on the non-standard √g, not √(−g). Nelson (1966), Guerra–Morato (1983) and, for the control-theory side, Kappen (2005) cover the real content better. |

| [LIT-007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-007.md) v2 | Quasi-quantization: classical statistical theories with an epistemic restriction | Spekkens (2014), [ARXIV-1409.5041](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.5041). | [LIT-019](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-019.md) v2 | Why interference phenomena do not capture the essence of quantum theory | Catani et al. (2021), [ARXIV-2111.13727](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13727). The paper models each mode of the interferometer as a classical bit pair (occupation N ∈ Z_2, phase Φ ∈ Z_2). The agent may know only one of N, Φ or N⊕Φ and must be maximally ignorant of the rest. Under that restriction, local and deterministic dynamics (beamsplitter: swap N_L with Φ_L⊕Φ_R) reproduce exactly the 50-50, ϕ ∈ {0, π} Mach–Zehnder statistics (output port L with probability 1 or 0; ½/½ with a which-way detector). The same holds for the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb tester (success probability ¼), delayed choice and the quantum eraser (interference within each P_A outcome class, none within each Q_A class). So this "TRAP" slice of interference phenomenology cannot, on its own, force wave–particle complementarity, observer-dependence or nonlocal/retrocausal influence. The paper leaves aside the phenomenology it concedes is nonclassical (unbalanced beamsplitters, the functional form of the duality relation, Hardy's interferometer). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-018); It is the worked, experiment-by-experiment defence of placing interference in the weakly nonclassical column of LIT-007's Table II, and it has the clearest statement of the Spekkens-school methodology (define classicality, formalize it, prove a no-go). The paper argues philosophically, not formally, that the quantum theory of open systems "GT" is more fundamental than standard closed-system quantum theory "ST". GT treats states as density operators that evolve, in general, non-unitarily, and it admits not-completely-positive maps. The ontic and epistemic cases each win only on a second, interpretation- or practice-laden criterion: OntFund-2 and EpFund-2. On the first, formal criteria (OntFund-1, EpFund-1) the two frameworks tie, and the authors say so because Stinespring dilation and dropping the Lindblad terms translate in both directions (§4.1, §4.2.1). | [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md) v2 | The Homological Nature of Entropy | Baudot & Bennequin (2015), DOI-10.3390/e17053253. On a finite probability space, take an information structure S (a set of partitions closed under joins that have a common refinement in S and containing the trivial partition) and a probability family Q complete for it. The information cohomology H*(S;Q) is computed by a Hochschild-type bar complex whose action is Shannon's averaged conditioning. If S is connected and "sufficiently rich" and cochains are measurable, then H¹ is one-dimensional and spanned by Shannon entropy (Thm 1). This makes entropy the unique measurable 1-cocycle, up to one multiplicative constant per connected component. In the unitary-invariant quantum case H¹_U = 0: Shannon entropy is the coboundary of minus the von Neumann entropy, which is the unique invariant 0-cochain with that property up to an additive constant (Thm 3). The tree ("arborescent") version again gives H¹ spanned by entropy (Thm 4). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 ([NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md)); the founding paper of information cohomology, with complete proofs of the degree-one results (Thms 1, 3, 4). Read it for those. Its broader programme (higher mutual informations as cocycles, super/sub-harmonicity, max-entropy discrimination) is sketched or deferred here to unpublished companion papers. |

The paper argues, with no new theorem, that the Lombardi–da Costa ontology of properties for quantum mechanics can be stated in Krause's quasi-set theory Q. On that ontology a system is a bundle of I-type-properties (instances of universal type-properties, represented by the algebra of observables) with no principle of individuality. For each property instance, the indiscernible instances form a qset U([Π]). An atomic bundle is any qset x with qc(x ∩ U) = 1 for each U; the Axiom of Choice in Q guarantees one exists. The bundle's kind is Q(B) = {x ∈ P(Q) \| R(x)}, whose members are all indiscernible. N particles are a subqset N(B) ⊂ Q(B) with qc = N, a definite number with no labels (§6, pp. 19–22). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-127.md)); worth reading as a short, clear bridge between the modal-Hamiltonian "ontology of properties" (Lombardi et al.) and quasi-set theory (French & Krause 2006). Gao argues first that ψ is real. His case uses protective measurements, which yield ⟨A⟩ on a single system with certainty, in three versions (ch. 4): one in the ontological-models framework using preparation non-contextuality, two he says need no auxiliary assumption, and one that uses a new criterion of reality. He then argues that ψ describes random discontinuous motion (RDM) of N point particles in 3-space: \|ψ\|² is the density with which each particle is present at each instant, and ψ is a single-case propensity. The main support is that the charge density \|ψ\|²Q, which protective measurement shows to exist, has no self-interaction (chs. 6–7). If the Born probabilities come from RDM, collapse is real. Gao proposes an energy-conserving, Planck-time-discrete collapse model: Pᵢ(t+t_P) = Pᵢ(t) + (ΔE/E_P)[δ_{EsEi} − Pᵢ(t)], giving τ_c ≈ ħE_P/(ΔE)² (ch. 8). Combined with relativity, it requires a detectable preferred Lorentz frame (ch. 9). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-140); worth reading as the fullest single statement of the protective-measurement argument for ψ-reality and of the RDM ontology. Its chapters 2, 3, 7.1 and 8.5 are also a well-referenced critical survey of ψ-epistemic, nomological, configuration-space-realist, Penrose and CSL views. Its central premises are contested (see Limitations), its collapse model is unconfirmed, and chapters 8–9 are openly speculative. |

A programmatic essay, not a result paper. Subsystems (tensor factorisations H = H_S ⊗ H_E or ⨂_α H_α), classicality and space are to be selected afterwards as rare structure that suits the dynamics. The only uniqueness he reports is for local factorisations, and it rests on a cited theorem (Cotler et al. 2019). Wave-function realism falsifies spatiotemporal-domain closure (STC) but is compatible with fundamental-physical closure (FPC), so there is no "trans-domain causal breach". The physicalist is left with a dilemma: STC is too narrow, and FPC needs an independent criterion of physicality plus a dynamical-to-causal bridge. French answers Howard's objection that QFT's unitarily inequivalent representations leave the structural realist with non-isomorphic, competing structures. He offers two routes. The first is to adopt cut-off "conventional" QFT with Wallace, on which the inequivalence is an artefact or harmless. The second is to follow Ruetsche's Swiss Army Knife and treat the algebra as a modal structure spanning all representations. On that reading spontaneous symmetry breaking preserves the symmetry across the degenerate vacua, and the DHR analysis derives quantum statistics from the algebra. Every step is an informal argument layered on others' technical results; the paper proves nothing itself. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md)); worth reading as a leading ontic structural realist's worked response to the strongest physics-based objection to OSR beyond finite-dimensional QM, and for its clear staging of the Wallace–Fraser and algebraic versus Hilbert-space debates. Morganti argues from a survey rather than proving anything. What OSR gets right about symmetry, entanglement and particle kinds is better captured by "metaphysical coherentism": object-like entities (in one domain) stand in symmetric *partial* ontological dependence on one another. Because it is the same across interpretations, he calls it "interpretation-independent" (p. 12). Where ψ needs a realist reading, it should be read as intrinsic dispositions of events. Esfeld et al.'s view has the opposite structure: bare matter points plus a single holistic power of the universal configuration. Rovelli restates RQM as an ontology of sparse relative facts, which arise in interactions and are labelled by the interacting systems. Its one technical rule is that an amplitude W(b,a) gives the probability P = \|W\|² only when a and b are relative to the same system. That rule removes the clash between P_collapse = Σᵢ\|W(c,bᵢ)\|²\|W(bᵢ,a)\|² and P_unitary = \|ΣᵢW(c,bᵢ)W(bᵢ,a)\|² (eqs. 2–4). The book gives a formal Schema: a duality is an isomorphism between the "model roots" (state space, quantities, dynamics) of two models of a common-core bare theory, with values and dynamics matching. It pairs this with an interpretative condition: duals are physically equivalent iff (A) they are duals and (B) i1 = i2∘d. On that basis it argues four things. First, there are no genuine cases of in-principle underdetermination in the examples, and a cautious realist can commit to the common core. Second, dualities do not favour structural realism. On this view it is an ingredient that "partially realizes" the law, not a law and not a material field. So its time-dependence and non-uniqueness (a phase shift, a density matrix) are harmless, it counts as non-epistemic and ontic, and it can take part in constructive explanation.
